the-dark-eye.rule.derived-characteristic.name: Derived characteristics

the-dark-eye.rule.fate-points-at-start.name: Fate Points at start

the-dark-eye.rule.familiar-soul-bond.name: familiar soul-bond

the-dark-eye.rule.sleep-is-a-divine-gift.name: Sleep is a divine gift

the-dark-eye.rule.dwarven-resistance-to-.name: Dwarven resistance to magic

effect.summary: Dwarves are less vulnerable to magic because of natural resistance.

the-dark-eye.rule.dwarven-resistance-to-.cost_or_limit: The resistance is general but not quantified here

effect.summary: Women may choose adopted daughters or daughters-in-law as heirs instead of naming their natural children.

the-dark-eye.rule.bornish-peasant-clothi.name: Bornish peasant clothing restrictions

the-dark-eye.rule.ranged-defense-penalti.blocked_reason: The defense restrictions and modifiers are playable.

the-dark-eye.rule.multiple-defenses-per-.name: Multiple defenses per round

effect.summary: Each additional defense in a round takes a cumulative penalty of 3; only Fate Point characters normally make multiple defenses.

the-dark-eye.rule.multiple-defenses-per-.cost_or_limit: Penalties reset at the next round; different defense modes share the penalty.
the-dark-eye.rule.multiple-defenses-per-.combines: Special abilities, spells, and liturgical chants may allow additional defenses.
the-dark-eye.rule.multiple-defenses-per-.blocked_reason: The limit and cumulative modifiers are playable.

the-dark-eye.rule.ranged-defense-critica.name: Ranged defense critical success

effect.summary: A confirmed natural 1 on defense prevents the usual penalty on the next defense; an unconfirmed 1 reduces that next penalty.

the-dark-eye.rule.ranged-defense-critica.combines: Applies to the next defense in the same round.
the-dark-eye.rule.ranged-defense-critica.blocked_reason: The confirmation and penalty adjustment are playable.

the-dark-eye.rule.ranged-defense-botch.name: Ranged defense botch

effect.summary: An unconfirmed natural 20 on defense inflicts 1D6+2 damage ignoring armor; a confirmed result is a simple failure.

the-dark-eye.rule.ranged-defense-botch.combines: An optional table can replace the default damage.
the-dark-eye.rule.ranged-defense-botch.blocked_reason: The roll and consequences are playable.

the-dark-eye.rule.ranged-damage-and-armo.name: Ranged damage and armor

effect.summary: Subtract protection from rolled missile damage, then subtract remaining damage from life points.

the-dark-eye.rule.ranged-damage-and-armo.cost_or_limit: Damage cannot reduce the target below the result of the calculation.

the-dark-eye.rule.low-life-points.name: Low Life Points

effect.summary: Losing each quarter of life points causes Pain; at 0 or fewer, a character is mortally wounded and soon dies without immediate treatment.

the-dark-eye.rule.low-life-points.cost_or_limit: Pain triggers at quarter-loss thresholds and at 5 or fewer LP.
the-dark-eye.rule.low-life-points.go_wrong: Untreated mortal wounds lead to death.
the-dark-eye.rule.low-life-points.blocked_reason: Mortality and death need a character life-state capability beyond the basic effect grammar.

the-dark-eye.rule.ranged-weapon-reload-t.name: Ranged weapon reload time

effect.summary: Ranged weapons require their listed actions to prepare; after reloading, an attack usually costs another action, except a loaded crossbow fires with a free action.

the-dark-eye.rule.ranged-weapon-reload-t.cost_or_limit: Zero-action reloads still cost a free action; reloads over one action are long actions.
the-dark-eye.rule.ranged-weapon-reload-t.go_wrong: An interrupted long action must be aborted.
the-dark-eye.rule.ranged-weapon-reload-t.blocked_reason: The preparation and action requirements are playable.

the-dark-eye.rule.projectile-recovery.name: Projectile recovery

effect.summary: Recovered arrows have a one-in-six chance of reuse; bolts and bullets have a two-in-six chance.

the-dark-eye.rule.projectile-recovery.cost_or_limit: Optional rule; failed rolls make ammunition unusable.
the-dark-eye.rule.projectile-recovery.combines: Missiles may also be damaged on impact.
the-dark-eye.rule.projectile-recovery.blocked_reason: Projectile usability requires tracking item state and depletion.

the-dark-eye.rule.bow-stringing.name: Bow stringing

effect.summary: Stringing a bow takes four actions during which no other actions can be taken.

the-dark-eye.rule.bow-stringing.combines: Crossbow string replacement takes several minutes as a long action.

the-dark-eye.rule.reusable-thrown-weapon.name: Reusable thrown weapons

effect.summary: Thrown weapons can normally be collected and used again immediately.

the-dark-eye.rule.reusable-thrown-weapon.cost_or_limit: They must be gathered after use.
the-dark-eye.rule.reusable-thrown-weapon.blocked_reason: Recovery is a basic item interaction.

the-dark-eye.rule.special-maneuver-limit.name: Special maneuver limit

effect.summary: A combatant can use one special maneuver per action and combine at most one basic and one special maneuver.

the-dark-eye.rule.special-maneuver-limit.cost_or_limit: One maneuver of each permitted category at most.
the-dark-eye.rule.special-maneuver-limit.combines: Applicable techniques may share a purchased special ability.

the-dark-eye.rule.two-weapon-combat.name: Two-weapon combat

effect.summary: Attacking and parrying with two weapons incurs penalties that can be reduced by the corresponding special ability.

the-dark-eye.rule.two-weapon-combat.cost_or_limit: The second level removes the penalties.
the-dark-eye.rule.two-weapon-combat.combines: Relevant weapons include those covered by the listed combat techniques.
the-dark-eye.rule.two-weapon-combat.blocked_reason: The penalties and reductions are playable.

the-dark-eye.rule.spell-and-ritual-metho.name: Spell and ritual methods

effect.summary: Spellcasting is usually quick, while rituals take longer and can produce stronger effects, summon beings, or create artifacts.

the-dark-eye.rule.spell-and-ritual-metho.cost_or_limit: Rituals may require hours or days.
the-dark-eye.rule.spell-and-ritual-metho.combines: Rituals can summon beings from other Spheres or make artifacts.
the-dark-eye.rule.spell-and-ritual-metho.blocked_reason: Summoning creatures from other Spheres requires a summon capability outside the basic effect grammar.

the-dark-eye.rule.arcane-energy-expendit.name: Arcane energy expenditure

effect.summary: Spells consume a limited reserve of arcane energy; a spell costing more than the caster has automatically fails.

the-dark-eye.rule.arcane-energy-expendit.cost_or_limit: Spell costs vary; energy is limited.
the-dark-eye.rule.arcane-energy-expendit.where_from: The magical world around the caster
the-dark-eye.rule.arcane-energy-expendit.combines: Spell power and effect may depend on remaining spell points.
the-dark-eye.rule.arcane-energy-expendit.blocked_reason: The resource cost and failure condition are playable.

the-dark-eye.rule.arcane-energy-regenera.name: Arcane energy regeneration

effect.summary: Spellcasters normally regain 1D6 arcane energy during each Regeneration Phase.

the-dark-eye.rule.arcane-energy-regenera.cost_or_limit: Regeneration amount may be increased by advantages or special abilities.
the-dark-eye.rule.arcane-energy-regenera.where_from: Magical energy in the surrounding world

the-dark-eye.rule.permanent-arcane-energ.name: Permanent arcane energy

effect.summary: Infusing an object to make magical power permanent costs some of the caster’s arcane energy permanently.

the-dark-eye.rule.permanent-arcane-energ.cost_or_limit: The lost energy does not regenerate normally.
the-dark-eye.rule.permanent-arcane-energ.go_wrong: The caster permanently loses part of their reserve.
the-dark-eye.rule.permanent-arcane-energ.blocked_reason: A lasting power stored in an object requires item-bound power and its carrying rules.

the-dark-eye.rule.magic-properties.name: Magic properties

effect.summary: Spells are classified by properties according to similarities in their effects and mechanisms.

the-dark-eye.rule.magic-properties.cost_or_limit: Each spell has an associated property.
the-dark-eye.rule.magic-properties.combines: Properties include anti-magic, clairvoyance, demonic, elemental, healing, illusion, influence, object, spheres, telekinesis, transformation, and temporal.
the-dark-eye.rule.magic-properties.blocked_reason: Classification alone does not require an additional effect capability.

the-dark-eye.rule.arcane-energy-ae.name: Arcane Energy (AE)

effect.summary: Only beings with Spellcaster can use AE, and magical actions consume it.

the-dark-eye.rule.arcane-energy-ae.cost_or_limit: Each action costs a specified amount.
the-dark-eye.rule.arcane-energy-ae.blocked_reason: This resource rule is directly playable.

the-dark-eye.rule.iron-ban.name: Iron Ban

effect.summary: Carried iron penalizes spell checks and reduces the next AE recovery.

the-dark-eye.rule.iron-ban.cost_or_limit: Each 2 full pounds gives a casting penalty of 1; carrying that amount for over an hour reduces next-phase AE recovery by 1.
the-dark-eye.rule.iron-ban.blocked_reason: The stated effects are costs and limits that can be applied directly.

the-dark-eye.rule.only-living-organic-bo.name: Only living organic bodies can be transformed

effect.summary: Transformation magic affects living organic bodies, not equipment or supernatural nonliving beings.

the-dark-eye.rule.only-living-organic-bo.cost_or_limit: Golems, undead, demons, and elementals are unaffected; equipment is not transformed.
the-dark-eye.rule.only-living-organic-bo.blocked_reason: This is a target restriction, not an unsupported effect.

the-dark-eye.rule.illusions-are-unreal.name: Illusions are unreal

effect.summary: Illusions have no weight, cannot affect objects or cause damage, and cannot be hot, cold, or create light.

the-dark-eye.rule.illusions-are-unreal.cost_or_limit: Changing illusions require concentration; they cannot act independently or think.
the-dark-eye.rule.illusions-are-unreal.mind: Illusions have no mind and do not react independently.
the-dark-eye.rule.illusions-are-unreal.combines: Illusions can be detected by a competitive Perception check.
the-dark-eye.rule.illusions-are-unreal.blocked_reason: These are limits on the illusion effect.

the-dark-eye.rule.permanent-loss-of-ae.name: Permanent Loss of AE

effect.summary: AE spent to keep an object’s magic permanent or semi-permanent reduces maximum AE and does not regenerate.

the-dark-eye.rule.permanent-loss-of-ae.cost_or_limit: Spent permanent AE can be bought back for 2 AP per AE.
the-dark-eye.rule.permanent-loss-of-ae.go_wrong: The spent AE does not regenerate.
the-dark-eye.rule.permanent-loss-of-ae.who_may: Spellcasters using rituals to imbue objects.
the-dark-eye.rule.permanent-loss-of-ae.combines: Used to preserve magic in an object.
the-dark-eye.rule.permanent-loss-of-ae.mechanism: Permanent resource loss for item enchantment
the-dark-eye.rule.permanent-loss-of-ae.blocked_reason: The rule concerns powers stored in objects and the resource required to maintain them.

the-dark-eye.rule.spell-effects-do-not-s.name: Spell effects do not stack

effect.summary: When supernatural effects with the same outcome overlap, only the strongest applies.

the-dark-eye.rule.spell-effects-do-not-s.cost_or_limit: Applies even when the effects come from different supernatural sources.
the-dark-eye.rule.spell-effects-do-not-s.who_may: Applies to spells, elixirs, miracles, and liturgical effects.
the-dark-eye.rule.spell-effects-do-not-s.blocked_reason: Resolving competing supernatural effects requires a power-interaction rule.

the-dark-eye.rule.spellcasting-requires-.name: Spellcasting requires concentration

effect.summary: Interruptions can break a casting; some actions force the caster to abort, and damage may call for a concentration check.

the-dark-eye.rule.spellcasting-requires-.cost_or_limit: An interrupted or aborted spell generally costs half its usual AE.
the-dark-eye.rule.spellcasting-requires-.go_wrong: Loss of concentration makes the spell fail.
the-dark-eye.rule.spellcasting-requires-.combines: Self-Control (Ignore Distractions) checks can preserve concentration.
the-dark-eye.rule.spellcasting-requires-.blocked_reason: The rule is a casting limitation and resource cost.

the-dark-eye.rule.failed-spells-still-co.name: Failed spells still cost AE

effect.summary: A failed spell usually costs half its normal AE; a failed sustained spell also costs the first interval.

the-dark-eye.rule.failed-spells-still-co.cost_or_limit: A failed spell costs half; sustained failures cost basic AE plus the first interval.
the-dark-eye.rule.failed-spells-still-co.combines: Critical success costs half the normal AE.
the-dark-eye.rule.failed-spells-still-co.blocked_reason: This is a direct resource-cost rule.

the-dark-eye.rule.permanent-spell-durati.name: Permanent spell duration cannot normally be ended early

effect.summary: A spell’s effect normally remains until its listed duration expires.

the-dark-eye.rule.permanent-spell-durati.cost_or_limit: No ordinary early termination is allowed.
the-dark-eye.rule.permanent-spell-durati.combines: Ritual effects likewise cannot be ended prematurely.

the-dark-eye.rule.transformation-costs-s.name: Transformation costs scale with target weight

effect.summary: Whole-body transformation costs vary with target mass relative to an assumed human weight.

the-dark-eye.rule.transformation-costs-s.cost_or_limit: Half-human weight costs half; up to twice human weight doubles cost, with further scaling; cost cannot fall below half normal.
the-dark-eye.rule.transformation-costs-s.combines: The target’s weight changes cost, not the check penalty.
the-dark-eye.rule.transformation-costs-s.blocked_reason: This is a direct cost adjustment.

the-dark-eye.rule.summoned-creature-impr.name: Summoned creature improvements reduce service QL

effect.summary: A summoner can spend successful-check QL on creature improvements instead of services.

the-dark-eye.rule.summoned-creature-impr.cost_or_limit: Each listed improvement can be chosen only once.
the-dark-eye.rule.summoned-creature-impr.go_wrong: Spending QL on improvements leaves less QL for services.
the-dark-eye.rule.summoned-creature-impr.combines: Improvement choices cover offense, defense, speed, magic, resistance, mental, and physical abilities.
the-dark-eye.rule.summoned-creature-impr.blocked_reason: The rule operates on creatures brought into play by summoning.

the-dark-eye.rule.failed-demon-summoning.name: Failed Demon Summoning

effect.summary: A failed demon summoning can produce outcomes on a secret roll; a botch adds 15.

the-dark-eye.rule.failed-demon-summoning.cost_or_limit: The caster pays half the AE; outcomes depend on a d20 result.
the-dark-eye.rule.failed-demon-summoning.go_wrong: May yield hazards, uncontrolled demons, or an archdemon's attention.
the-dark-eye.rule.failed-demon-summoning.blocked_reason: This is a roll-based consequence rule.

the-dark-eye.rule.artifact-spell-activat.name: Artifact spell activation

effect.summary: Stored spells usually activate through a word or gesture and take effect next combat round after a check.

the-dark-eye.rule.artifact-spell-activat.cost_or_limit: Activation check uses attributes of 14 and a target number based on stored spell SP; variable duration and cost are chosen before enchantment.
the-dark-eye.rule.artifact-spell-activat.combines: Stored spell effect is not thereby a magical weapon
the-dark-eye.rule.artifact-spell-activat.blocked_reason: The rule requires an item to carry and activate a stored power.

the-dark-eye.rule.artifact-types-and-sto.name: Artifact types and stored power

effect.summary: Storage artifacts are used up, recharging artifacts replenish, and permanent artifacts do not diminish.

the-dark-eye.rule.artifact-types-and-sto.cost_or_limit: No artifact can contain more than seven charges.
the-dark-eye.rule.artifact-types-and-sto.blocked_reason: The rule defines power storage, recharge, permanence, and a charge cap.

the-dark-eye.rule.protective-and-warding.name: Protective and warding circle limits

effect.summary: Circles restrict movement but do not stop spells or simple thrown items; some powerful beings ignore them.

the-dark-eye.rule.protective-and-warding.cost_or_limit: They fail against high-ranking archdemon servants and elemental masters; smudging a circle ends it.
the-dark-eye.rule.protective-and-warding.go_wrong: A creature may smudge delicate signs with spells or nearby objects.
the-dark-eye.rule.protective-and-warding.who_may: Applies to magical beings and circle users
the-dark-eye.rule.protective-and-warding.blocked_reason: The rule concerns persistent spatial boundaries and their exceptions.

the-dark-eye.rule.permanent-ae-binding.name: Permanent AE binding

effect.summary: Artifact creators bind permanent AE into objects to establish a lasting magical matrix.

the-dark-eye.rule.permanent-ae-binding.cost_or_limit: Permanent AE is spent and remains bound in the object.
the-dark-eye.rule.permanent-ae-binding.blocked_reason: The rule defines permanent power transfer into an item.

the-dark-eye.rule.spell-storage-artifact.name: Spell Storage Artifact creation

effect.summary: A creator prepares an item with Arcanovi and casts each stored spell immediately afterward.

the-dark-eye.rule.spell-storage-artifact.cost_or_limit: Repeated spell activations add penalties; modifications are forbidden; one tenth of spent AE is permanently lost; maximum seven charges.
the-dark-eye.rule.spell-storage-artifact.go_wrong: Any failed check ruins the enchantment, without permanent AE loss.
the-dark-eye.rule.spell-storage-artifact.blocked_reason: The rule covers power transfer, charges, and depletion.

the-dark-eye.rule.self-charging-artifact.name: Self-charging Artifact costs and penalties

effect.summary: More frequent recharging increases checks and AE costs: monthly costs five times, weekly ten times, and daily twenty-five times the spell cost.

the-dark-eye.rule.self-charging-artifact.cost_or_limit: Recharge interval also sets escalating penalties to both checks.
the-dark-eye.rule.self-charging-artifact.blocked_reason: It describes an item regenerating stored power and the associated costs.

the-dark-eye.rule.artifact-size.name: Artifact size

effect.summary: Small objects restrict the number and improvement cost of spells they can hold.

the-dark-eye.rule.artifact-size.cost_or_limit: A small object holds at most one spell of improvement cost A; very small objects add an Arcanovi penalty of two.
the-dark-eye.rule.artifact-size.blocked_reason: The rule sets a capacity limit for powers carried by an item.

the-dark-eye.rule.material-effects-on-en.name: Material effects on enchantment

effect.summary: Iron or steel makes enchantment harder, while suitable materials can reduce cost or improve a ritual check.

the-dark-eye.rule.material-effects-on-en.cost_or_limit: At least fifty percent iron or steel gives a penalty of two; suitable materials cost 100 silverthalers per point of permanent AE saved, at most half the permanent cost.
the-dark-eye.rule.material-effects-on-en.go_wrong: Materials are consumed if the project fails.
the-dark-eye.rule.material-effects-on-en.blocked_reason: The rule depends on particular material composition and cannot be represented by the basic effect grammar.

the-dark-eye.rule.artifact-side-effects.name: Artifact side effects

effect.summary: A low-quality Arcanovi result can cause a hidden, randomly determined side effect.

the-dark-eye.rule.artifact-side-effects.cost_or_limit: Triggered when Arcanovi QL is no more than one.
the-dark-eye.rule.artifact-side-effects.go_wrong: Possible results include an inhabiting spirit, altered physical properties, odd activation conditions, harmful owner influence, or delayed hazards.
the-dark-eye.rule.artifact-side-effects.mind: The owner may develop fear of loss and overprotect the item.
the-dark-eye.rule.artifact-side-effects.mechanism: Random artifact drift and side effects
the-dark-eye.rule.artifact-side-effects.blocked_reason: The table includes delayed, persistent, and mind-affecting side effects beyond the basic grammar.

the-dark-eye.rule.stacked-alchemical-eff.name: Stacked Alchemical Effects

effect.summary: When supernatural effects overlap, only the strongest effect applies.

the-dark-eye.rule.stacked-alchemical-eff.cost_or_limit: Applies to effects on the same person or object, including spells, elixirs, miracles, and chants.
the-dark-eye.rule.stacked-alchemical-eff.who_may: All subjects of overlapping supernatural effects
the-dark-eye.rule.stacked-alchemical-eff.blocked_reason: The rule resolves competing effects by comparing their strength.

the-dark-eye.rule.summoned-creature-serv.name: Summoned creature services

effect.summary: A summoned creature must perform at least one service, gains additional services from QL, and disappears when services run out.

the-dark-eye.rule.summoned-creature-serv.cost_or_limit: Generally one remaining service is lost each sunrise; service types have their own duration and minimums.
the-dark-eye.rule.summoned-creature-serv.go_wrong: A creature may not perform every service type.
the-dark-eye.rule.summoned-creature-serv.combines: Labor, advice, ability use, combat, espionage, search, and guard
the-dark-eye.rule.summoned-creature-serv.blocked_reason: The rule involves a summoned autonomous creature following orders and spending services.

the-dark-eye.rule.elixir-brewing-limits.name: Elixir brewing limits

effect.summary: Brewing requires a formula, ingredients, and a laboratory; a character can brew at most one elixir per day.

the-dark-eye.rule.elixir-brewing-limits.cost_or_limit: Ingredient level caps elixir quality; laboratory rating modifies checks; AE infusion grants a limited bonus.
the-dark-eye.rule.elixir-brewing-limits.go_wrong: A failed check destroys ingredients and may cause a mishap.
the-dark-eye.rule.elixir-brewing-limits.combines: Alchemy checks, laboratory quality, ingredients, and optional AE
the-dark-eye.rule.elixir-brewing-limits.mechanism: Crafting check, quality cap, and failure table
the-dark-eye.rule.elixir-brewing-limits.blocked_reason: The procedure is a standard check with clear limits and outcomes.

the-dark-eye.rule.elixir-onset.name: Elixir onset

effect.summary: Elixirs generally take effect at the beginning of the combat round after consumption.

the-dark-eye.rule.elixir-onset.cost_or_limit: Specific potion descriptions may override this timing.
the-dark-eye.rule.elixir-onset.blocked_reason: The rule defines a simple timing delay.

the-dark-eye.rule.magical-traditions.name: Magical traditions

effect.summary: Learning a spell from an unfamiliar tradition imposes a penalty and prevents spell modifications.

the-dark-eye.rule.magical-traditions.cost_or_limit: Penalty of two; learning a tradition requires years of commitment and is especially difficult later in life.
the-dark-eye.rule.magical-traditions.mind: Requires realigning one's view of self and world.
the-dark-eye.rule.magical-traditions.where_from: Guild mages, witches, elves, and other traditions
the-dark-eye.rule.magical-traditions.combines: A spell retains its original tradition even when taught by someone from another tradition
the-dark-eye.rule.magical-traditions.blocked_reason: The rule changes how a power works based on its tradition and user.

the-dark-eye.rule.staff-enchantment-capa.name: Staff enchantment capacity

effect.summary: Each staff enchantment occupies volume points, and insufficient capacity prevents adding more.

the-dark-eye.rule.staff-enchantment-capa.cost_or_limit: Typical staff capacity is 18 volume points.
the-dark-eye.rule.staff-enchantment-capa.blocked_reason: This rule depends on quantifying powers stored in an item.

the-dark-eye.rule.staff-enchantment-perm.name: Staff enchantment permanence

effect.summary: An enchantment placed on a staff cannot later be removed.

the-dark-eye.rule.staff-enchantment-perm.combines: Some enchantments require another enchantment first.
the-dark-eye.rule.staff-enchantment-perm.blocked_reason: The rule governs persistent powers attached to an item.

the-dark-eye.rule.staff-enchantment-acti.name: Staff enchantment activation

effect.summary: Usually only one staff enchantment may operate at once, with specified focus exceptions.

the-dark-eye.rule.staff-enchantment-acti.cost_or_limit: Temporary effects take an action to activate; some cost AE, and a mage may abort one with a free action.
the-dark-eye.rule.staff-enchantment-acti.combines: Binding of the Staff and the two focus enchantments are exceptions to the one-at-a-time limit.
the-dark-eye.rule.staff-enchantment-acti.blocked_reason: The rule coordinates concurrent item-bound powers and their activation.

the-dark-eye.rule.flying-balm-restrictio.name: Flying balm restriction

effect.summary: Flying balm makes one chosen wooden object controllably fly for one year, but does not alter its physical qualities.

the-dark-eye.rule.flying-balm-restrictio.cost_or_limit: Made only at the annual Witches’ Night; each witch gets enough for one object, applies it there, and can control only that object. Replacement must wait until the next gathering.
the-dark-eye.rule.flying-balm-restrictio.go_wrong: Treated objects remain destructible and suffer ordinary item damage.
the-dark-eye.rule.flying-balm-restrictio.who_may: Witches with the Tradition Witch ability
the-dark-eye.rule.flying-balm-restrictio.combines: Flying balm must be applied during the gathering.
the-dark-eye.rule.flying-balm-restrictio.blocked_reason: The rule gives a mundane object a limited-duration bound movement power.

the-dark-eye.rule.curse-timing-and-deliv.name: Curse timing and delivery

effect.summary: Curses usually take effect after 24 hours and can be delivered directly, through a familiar, or remotely using a body part as a link.

the-dark-eye.rule.curse-timing-and-deliv.cost_or_limit: Remote casting requires midnight and a sleeping target; ordinary range is at most 64 yards.
the-dark-eye.rule.curse-timing-and-deliv.mind: Targets learn how to remove a remote curse through dreams.
the-dark-eye.rule.curse-timing-and-deliv.who_may: Witches; curses are taught only to witches
the-dark-eye.rule.curse-timing-and-deliv.combines: Familiars can deliver curses with Curse Bringer.
the-dark-eye.rule.curse-timing-and-deliv.blocked_reason: Curses impose diverse delayed conditions and require ongoing or conditional resolution.

the-dark-eye.rule.lifting-a-curse.name: Lifting a curse

effect.summary: A curse may end when its demands are met, when its witch spends 3 AE to revoke it, or when the witch dies.

the-dark-eye.rule.lifting-a-curse.cost_or_limit: Liturgical chants and anti-magic may also help.
the-dark-eye.rule.lifting-a-curse.who_may: The cursed target or the witch, depending on the means
the-dark-eye.rule.lifting-a-curse.combines: The witch may state demands as part of the curse.
the-dark-eye.rule.lifting-a-curse.blocked_reason: The rule requires a persistent curse with several possible termination triggers.

the-dark-eye.rule.sustaining-spells.name: Sustaining spells

effect.summary: Some spells can be sustained by paying their upkeep cost at each interval; maintaining them requires concentration.

the-dark-eye.rule.sustaining-spells.cost_or_limit: Each sustained spell imposes a check penalty; a failed check costs the base spell cost plus its first interval.
the-dark-eye.rule.sustaining-spells.go_wrong: A failed check ends the effort and charges the specified AE.
the-dark-eye.rule.sustaining-spells.combines: Multiple sustained spells increase the penalty.
the-dark-eye.rule.sustaining-spells.blocked_reason: The rule defines ordinary duration upkeep and its cost.

the-dark-eye.rule.cantrip-rules.name: Cantrip rules

effect.summary: Cantrips are minor effects with fixed QL, cost, and action time, cast without a check.

the-dark-eye.rule.cantrip-rules.cost_or_limit: Each costs 1 AE and 1 AP, takes one action, has QL 1, and cannot be modified.
the-dark-eye.rule.cantrip-rules.combines: All cantrips are available across traditions.
the-dark-eye.rule.cantrip-rules.blocked_reason: This defines a simple power’s cost and activation.

the-dark-eye.rule.odem-check-modifiers.name: Odem check modifiers

effect.summary: Odem checks gain or lose modifiers based on magical energy and the target's supernatural type.

the-dark-eye.rule.odem-check-modifiers.cost_or_limit: Bound and effective AE and creature type set the listed modifiers.
the-dark-eye.rule.odem-check-modifiers.blocked_reason: This rule modifies a check and is not itself an effect requiring a missing capability.

the-dark-eye.rule.permanent-ae-in-spellb.name: Permanent AE in Spellblade Spiritspear

effect.summary: One twentieth of the ritual's AE cost is permanent AE and can be regained only under the separate permanent-AE rules.

the-dark-eye.rule.permanent-ae-in-spellb.cost_or_limit: The permanent portion is 1/20 of the ritual's AE cost.
the-dark-eye.rule.permanent-ae-in-spellb.go_wrong: The spent AE is permanently bound rather than freely recoverable.
the-dark-eye.rule.permanent-ae-in-spellb.who_may: Applies to users of the ritual
the-dark-eye.rule.permanent-ae-in-spellb.blocked_reason: The rule describes a lasting cost and requires no unsupported effect capability.

the-dark-eye.rule.limited-karma.name: Limited Karma

effect.summary: A god may suspend a Blessed One’s recovery of karma points after a severe violation until the god is satisfied.

the-dark-eye.rule.limited-karma.cost_or_limit: The GM decides whether penance can restore divine trust.
the-dark-eye.rule.limited-karma.blocked_reason: This is a rule about resource recovery and can be modeled directly.

the-dark-eye.rule.karmic-energy-and-karm.name: Karmic Energy and Karma Points

effect.summary: Gods grant karma points to fuel liturgical chants and ceremonies; Blessed Ones normally regain 1D6 spent points per regeneration phase.

the-dark-eye.rule.karmic-energy-and-karm.cost_or_limit: A chant cannot be performed if its cost exceeds the available points.
the-dark-eye.rule.karmic-energy-and-karm.go_wrong: An unsuccessful chant still consumes half its normal cost.
the-dark-eye.rule.karmic-energy-and-karm.where_from: A patron god grants the resource.
the-dark-eye.rule.karmic-energy-and-karm.combines: Advantages and special abilities can increase recovery.
the-dark-eye.rule.karmic-energy-and-karm.blocked_reason: A points pool with costs and recovery can be tracked directly.

the-dark-eye.rule.blessed-traditions.name: Blessed Traditions

effect.summary: Blessed Ones can learn chants from their own tradition and general chants, but cannot use chants of an unfamiliar tradition.

the-dark-eye.rule.blessed-traditions.cost_or_limit: Access is limited by religious tradition.
the-dark-eye.rule.blessed-traditions.blocked_reason: A restriction on which powers a character may use is directly implementable.

the-dark-eye.rule.target-categories.name: Target Categories

effect.summary: A chant fails if its target is outside the category it permits.

the-dark-eye.rule.target-categories.cost_or_limit: The target must also remain in range and in view when required.
the-dark-eye.rule.target-categories.blocked_reason: This is a target eligibility restriction.

the-dark-eye.rule.liturgical-modificatio.name: Liturgical modifications

effect.summary: A Blessed One may modify casting time, range, cost, or casting difficulty, with available choices based on skill rating.

the-dark-eye.rule.liturgical-modificatio.cost_or_limit: One modification per four full SR; a modification type cannot be chosen twice, and a category shifts at most one increment.
the-dark-eye.rule.liturgical-modificatio.go_wrong: Some modifications impose a check penalty.
the-dark-eye.rule.liturgical-modificatio.combines: Modifications can be combined when they are different types.
the-dark-eye.rule.liturgical-modificatio.blocked_reason: The effects are adjustments to cost, range, time, and check difficulty.

the-dark-eye.rule.liturgical-concentrati.name: Liturgical concentration

effect.summary: An interruption or voluntary break in concentration ends a chant and charges the failure cost.

the-dark-eye.rule.liturgical-concentrati.cost_or_limit: The caster must maintain concentration through casting and any sustained effect.
the-dark-eye.rule.liturgical-concentrati.go_wrong: The chant fails and still costs KP.
the-dark-eye.rule.liturgical-concentrati.who_may: Blessed Ones casting or sustaining chants
the-dark-eye.rule.liturgical-concentrati.combines: Distractions may require a Self-Control check.
the-dark-eye.rule.liturgical-concentrati.blocked_reason: A concentration requirement and interruption consequence can be modeled directly.

the-dark-eye.rule.failed-liturgical-chan.name: Failed liturgical chants

effect.summary: A failed chant still consumes half its ordinary KP cost; failure while sustaining costs the base amount plus the first interval.

the-dark-eye.rule.failed-liturgical-chan.cost_or_limit: Costs are deducted from the caster’s KP pool.
the-dark-eye.rule.failed-liturgical-chan.go_wrong: Failure consumes resources without producing the effect.
the-dark-eye.rule.failed-liturgical-chan.blocked_reason: Resource loss on failure is directly implementable.

the-dark-eye.rule.permanent-loss-of-karm.name: Permanent Loss of Karma Points

effect.summary: Some deeds permanently reduce maximum KP, though the lost capacity can be bought back with adventure points.

the-dark-eye.rule.permanent-loss-of-karm.cost_or_limit: Buying back a point costs 2 adventure points.
the-dark-eye.rule.permanent-loss-of-karm.go_wrong: The maximum does not regenerate naturally.
the-dark-eye.rule.permanent-loss-of-karm.who_may: Characters who perform actions requiring permanent KP
the-dark-eye.rule.permanent-loss-of-karm.where_from: Certain divine acts, such as creating sacred artifacts
the-dark-eye.rule.permanent-loss-of-karm.blocked_reason: Permanent maximum-resource changes and later purchase are directly trackable.

the-dark-eye.rule.size-and-kp-cost.name: Size and KP Cost

effect.summary: For body-affecting chants, KP cost scales with target weight relative to a human baseline.

the-dark-eye.rule.size-and-kp-cost.cost_or_limit: Half cost at up to half human weight; double at up to twice; triple at up to three times; the check is unchanged.
the-dark-eye.rule.size-and-kp-cost.blocked_reason: A numeric cost multiplier based on size is directly implementable.

the-dark-eye.rule.stacking-liturgical-ef.name: Stacking Liturgical Effects

effect.summary: When supernatural effects of the same kind overlap, only the strongest one applies.

the-dark-eye.rule.stacking-liturgical-ef.cost_or_limit: Applies across spells, elixirs, miracles, and chants.
the-dark-eye.rule.stacking-liturgical-ef.blocked_reason: Selecting the strongest among overlapping supernatural effects requires explicit power-interaction logic.

the-dark-eye.rule.sacred-ground.name: Sacred ground

effect.summary: Ceremonies performed at temples or other holy sites receive a check bonus.

the-dark-eye.rule.sacred-ground.cost_or_limit: The site’s religious alignment determines the bonus or penalty.
the-dark-eye.rule.sacred-ground.go_wrong: Opposing or hostile holy sites can impose penalties.
the-dark-eye.rule.sacred-ground.where_from: Temples and sites sacred to gods
the-dark-eye.rule.sacred-ground.combines: Place and time modifiers can affect the same check, subject to the stated limits.
the-dark-eye.rule.sacred-ground.blocked_reason: A site-based modifier to a check is directly implementable.

the-dark-eye.rule.blessing-and-sanctific.name: Blessing and sanctification

effect.summary: Blessed Ones choose only god-pleasing items or places, and give them only to true believers.

the-dark-eye.rule.blessing-and-sanctific.cost_or_limit: Requires serious thought and a suitable recipient or subject.

the-dark-eye.rule.blessed-materials-harm.name: Blessed materials harm demons

effect.summary: Contact with blessed or sacred material harms demons manifested in the Third Sphere.

the-dark-eye.rule.blessed-materials-harm.cost_or_limit: Blessed material is destroyed after three CR of direct contact; sacred ground damages demons over time.
the-dark-eye.rule.blessed-materials-harm.go_wrong: The material is destroyed by prolonged contact.
the-dark-eye.rule.blessed-materials-harm.where_from: Blessed or sacred materials and ground
the-dark-eye.rule.blessed-materials-harm.combines: Directly opposed gods increase damage; twice-sanctified ground changes its damage interval.
the-dark-eye.rule.blessed-materials-harm.blocked_reason: The described damage and timing fit the basic effect grammar.

the-dark-eye.rule.sacred-weapons-against.name: Sacred weapons against demons

effect.summary: Sacred weapons damage demons normally, or deal double damage when sanctified by the directly opposed god.

the-dark-eye.rule.sacred-weapons-against.cost_or_limit: The damage bonus applies only to the demon’s directly opposed deity.
the-dark-eye.rule.sacred-weapons-against.combines: Damage is calculated before protection is subtracted.
the-dark-eye.rule.sacred-weapons-against.blocked_reason: A damage modifier can be represented with the basic effect grammar.

the-dark-eye.rule.desecration.name: Desecration

effect.summary: Repeated or extreme acts against a deity’s principles can remove an item’s or place’s sacred status.

the-dark-eye.rule.desecration.cost_or_limit: The GM determines whether desecration has occurred.
the-dark-eye.rule.desecration.go_wrong: Sacred ground or an object loses its sanctity.
the-dark-eye.rule.desecration.who_may: Acts by people can desecrate sacred things.
the-dark-eye.rule.desecration.where_from: The god whose sacred place or item is violated
the-dark-eye.rule.desecration.combines: Examples include repeated lawbreaking in a temple or using a sacred weapon dishonorably.
the-dark-eye.rule.desecration.blocked_reason: The effect depends on tracking and removing an item or place’s sacred state.

the-dark-eye.rule.divine-power-forms.name: Divine power forms

effect.summary: Blessings, chants, ceremonies, miracles, and great miracles are distinct forms; Blessed Ones may pray for great miracles but cannot cast them.

the-dark-eye.rule.divine-power-forms.cost_or_limit: Great miracles depend on the GM answering; only prayers are available to Blessed Ones.
the-dark-eye.rule.divine-power-forms.go_wrong: A plea may not be answered.
the-dark-eye.rule.divine-power-forms.combines: Ceremonies function like chants but take longer; miracles are quick, costly, and inflexible.
the-dark-eye.rule.divine-power-forms.blocked_reason: This defines access and categories rather than an unrepresented effect.

the-dark-eye.rule.sustaining-liturgical-.name: Sustaining liturgical chants

effect.summary: Sustaining some chants consumes additional KP each interval and requires concentration.

the-dark-eye.rule.sustaining-liturgical-.cost_or_limit: A failed check still costs the base KP plus the first interval; each sustained chant penalizes chant checks by 1.
the-dark-eye.rule.sustaining-liturgical-.go_wrong: A failed check consumes KP; loss of ability to pay ends the sustained effect.
the-dark-eye.rule.sustaining-liturgical-.combines: Intense concentration can hinder other actions.
the-dark-eye.rule.sustaining-liturgical-.blocked_reason: Periodic costs and concentration penalties are directly representable.

the-dark-eye.rule.tradition-access-to-ch.name: Tradition access to chants

effect.summary: Blessed Ones normally cannot use chants from other Traditions; general-aspect blessings are shared.

the-dark-eye.rule.tradition-access-to-ch.cost_or_limit: Access is normally restricted to one’s own Tradition.
the-dark-eye.rule.tradition-access-to-ch.combines: General-aspect blessings have versions for all Traditions.
the-dark-eye.rule.tradition-access-to-ch.blocked_reason: The game must enforce which characters may use which powers.

the-dark-eye.rule.rules-for-blessings.name: Rules for Blessings

effect.summary: Blessings resolve automatically at QL 1, cost 1 KP, take one action, and cannot use chant or ceremony modifications.

the-dark-eye.rule.rules-for-blessings.cost_or_limit: Learning one costs 1 AP; modifications are prohibited.
the-dark-eye.rule.rules-for-blessings.who_may: All Blessed Ones with access to the blessing
the-dark-eye.rule.rules-for-blessings.combines: Blessings are treated as special abilities.
the-dark-eye.rule.rules-for-blessings.blocked_reason: These are simple costs and procedure limits.

the-dark-eye.rule.regeneration-phase.name: Regeneration Phase

effect.summary: Rest and sleep for at least six hours allow recovery of life, arcane energy, and karma points.

the-dark-eye.rule.regeneration-phase.cost_or_limit: At most two phases per day; basic recovery is 1D6 per point type, modified by circumstances; totals cannot exceed current maximums.
the-dark-eye.rule.regeneration-phase.who_may: Characters missing LP, AE, or KP.
the-dark-eye.rule.regeneration-phase.combines: Poor rest can reduce or eliminate recovery; good lodging can improve it; iron carried reduces AE recovery; disease and poison prevent LP regeneration while active.
the-dark-eye.rule.regeneration-phase.blocked_reason: The recovery process is a game rule rather than an unrepresented world mechanism.

the-dark-eye.rule.weaker-regeneration.name: Weaker Regeneration

effect.summary: An optional realism rule removes LP regeneration bonuses and limits LP recovery to 1D3 per Regeneration Phase.

the-dark-eye.rule.weaker-regeneration.cost_or_limit: Optional rule; applies to LP regeneration.
the-dark-eye.rule.weaker-regeneration.combines: Replaces the normal LP regeneration rate and bonuses.
the-dark-eye.rule.weaker-regeneration.blocked_reason: This is a game procedure for recovery.

the-dark-eye.rule.life-saving-measures-a.name: Life-Saving Measures and Death

effect.summary: A mortally wounded character can be treated before a Constitution-based round limit; failed or absent treatment leads to death, while successful stabilization restores 1 LP.

the-dark-eye.rule.life-saving-measures-a.cost_or_limit: Treatment must begin within rounds equal to Constitution; stabilization takes 15 minutes and its check penalty depends on LP below zero; reaching Constitution points below zero causes immediate death.
the-dark-eye.rule.life-saving-measures-a.go_wrong: Failed stabilization without supernatural aid results in death; interruption leaves only the remaining treatment-time rounds.
the-dark-eye.rule.life-saving-measures-a.who_may: Mortally wounded characters and their rescuers.
the-dark-eye.rule.life-saving-measures-a.combines: Magic, potions, and other supernatural aid can prevent death.
the-dark-eye.rule.life-saving-measures-a.mechanism: Timed mortal-wound treatment and death threshold.
the-dark-eye.rule.life-saving-measures-a.blocked_reason: The rule maps to a timed treatment check and LP threshold.

the-dark-eye.rule.falling-damage.name: Falling Damage

effect.summary: Falls cause damage based on distance and ground, with Jumping checks and sometimes armor reducing the harm.

the-dark-eye.rule.falling-damage.cost_or_limit: Roll 1D6 per yard; apply ground modifiers; each QL on Body Control (Jumping) reduces damage by 2 DP.
the-dark-eye.rule.falling-damage.combines: Armor may reduce damage at the GM’s discretion.
the-dark-eye.rule.falling-damage.blocked_reason: The rule uses ordinary damage and skill checks.

the-dark-eye.rule.fire-and-acid-damage.name: Fire and Acid Damage

effect.summary: Fire or acid damages exposed body areas each combat round until the character escapes the threat.

the-dark-eye.rule.fire-and-acid-damage.cost_or_limit: Small areas take 1D3 DP, large areas 1D6, and the whole body 2D6 per round, ignoring protection; intense heat or strong acid doubles damage.
the-dark-eye.rule.fire-and-acid-damage.go_wrong: Characters may continue taking damage until clear; acid requires a diluting or neutralizing substance before a Body Control escape check is possible.
the-dark-eye.rule.fire-and-acid-damage.who_may: Characters exposed to fire or acid.
the-dark-eye.rule.fire-and-acid-damage.combines: Body Control checks, helpers, water, sand, or other materials can extinguish or neutralize the threat.
the-dark-eye.rule.fire-and-acid-damage.mechanism: Repeated exposure damage with escape checks.
the-dark-eye.rule.fire-and-acid-damage.blocked_reason: The rule maps to repeated damage and checks.

the-dark-eye.rule.suffocation-damage.name: Suffocation Damage

effect.summary: Lack of air causes Stupor over time, then recurring damage, and death after a Constitution-based duration.

the-dark-eye.rule.suffocation-damage.cost_or_limit: Gain one Stupor level every 25 combat rounds; after Constitution minutes, take 1D6 DP per round ignoring protection; death follows after that duration.
the-dark-eye.rule.suffocation-damage.go_wrong: Continued suffocation causes unconsciousness and death.
the-dark-eye.rule.suffocation-damage.who_may: Characters unable to get enough air.
the-dark-eye.rule.suffocation-damage.blocked_reason: The rule uses conditions, damage, and a death timer.

the-dark-eye.rule.poisons.name: Poisons

effect.summary: A poison check determines whether a poison takes full or reduced effect; exposure method and the victim’s resistance determine application.

the-dark-eye.rule.poisons.cost_or_limit: Poison attributes equal 10 plus level, with SR equal to level; one dose suits a medium creature, more is needed for larger creatures; poison cannot be applied to weapons during combat.
the-dark-eye.rule.poisons.go_wrong: A failed poison check reduces effects and duration; active poison prevents LP regeneration.
the-dark-eye.rule.poisons.mind: Some poisons cause confusion or hallucinations, depending on their entry.
the-dark-eye.rule.poisons.where_from: Poison source and exposure type determine how it enters the victim.
the-dark-eye.rule.poisons.combines: Weapon poison can be delivered only by bladed or stabbing weapons and is limited in duration and attacks; Treat Poison can identify it and find an antidote.
the-dark-eye.rule.poisons.mechanism: Resistance check with level-based effects and duration.
the-dark-eye.rule.poisons.blocked_reason: The rule uses checks, damage, and conditions.

the-dark-eye.rule.short-term-effectivene.name: Short Term Effectiveness of Weapon Poisons

effect.summary: Weapon poison must be applied shortly before combat and only delivers through a damaging hit that penetrates protection.

the-dark-eye.rule.short-term-effectivene.cost_or_limit: Works only on bladed or stabbing weapons, lasts no more than five attacks, and cannot be applied during combat.
the-dark-eye.rule.short-term-effectivene.go_wrong: If the first hit fails to pierce protection, later hits automatically fail to deliver the poison.
the-dark-eye.rule.short-term-effectivene.combines: Requires a successful hit that causes damage and pierces PRO.
the-dark-eye.rule.short-term-effectivene.mechanism: Limited-use weapon coating and delivery rule.
the-dark-eye.rule.short-term-effectivene.blocked_reason: The rule is a conditional application of a poison effect.

the-dark-eye.rule.preserving-poisons.name: Preserving Poisons

effect.summary: Poison weakens after three months and becomes harmless after six months regardless of storage.

the-dark-eye.rule.preserving-poisons.cost_or_limit: Reduced effects and duration after three months; no potency after six months.
the-dark-eye.rule.preserving-poisons.combines: Weakened poison uses the reduced effects and duration listed in its entry.
the-dark-eye.rule.preserving-poisons.blocked_reason: The rule is a straightforward time-based change in an item’s effectiveness.

the-dark-eye.rule.disease.name: Disease

effect.summary: A disease check determines the severity of an infection, with incubation before symptoms appear and failed checks producing weaker effects.

the-dark-eye.rule.disease.cost_or_limit: Disease attributes equal 10 plus level and SR equals level; Spirit or Toughness applies as a penalty.
the-dark-eye.rule.disease.go_wrong: A failed disease check causes reduced effects and duration.
the-dark-eye.rule.disease.mind: Some diseases cause fear, anxiety, confusion, or other mental symptoms.
the-dark-eye.rule.disease.combines: Treatment and cures can reduce progress or symptoms; active disease prevents LP regeneration.
the-dark-eye.rule.disease.mechanism: Infection chance, resistance check, incubation, and disease effects.
the-dark-eye.rule.disease.blocked_reason: The rule uses checks, damage, and conditions.

the-dark-eye.rule.healing-herbs-effect.name: Healing Herbs: Effect

effect.summary: Only the first healing herb used in a Regeneration Phase provides its effect, and additional doses of the same herb do not stack unless specified.

the-dark-eye.rule.healing-herbs-effect.cost_or_limit: One dose is enough for one person; amounts found depend on QL.
the-dark-eye.rule.healing-herbs-effect.go_wrong: Herb effects do not stack by default.
the-dark-eye.rule.healing-herbs-effect.combines: Applies to herb effects during a Regeneration Phase.
the-dark-eye.rule.healing-herbs-effect.blocked_reason: This is a straightforward limit on herb-use effects.

the-dark-eye.rule.cold-level-and-hypothe.name: Cold Level and Hypothermia

effect.summary: Cold Level minus protection and modifiers determines whether hypothermia accumulates; colder levels make it accrue faster, with severe levels causing unconsciousness and LP loss.

the-dark-eye.rule.cold-level-and-hypothe.cost_or_limit: Cold levels run I–IV; protective clothing reduces level, while wet clothes, wind, and blizzards raise it.
the-dark-eye.rule.cold-level-and-hypothe.go_wrong: At the coldest level, continued exposure can cause death.
the-dark-eye.rule.cold-level-and-hypothe.combines: Warm, dry surroundings remove one hypothermia level per Regeneration Phase.
the-dark-eye.rule.cold-level-and-hypothe.mechanism: Exposure thresholds and accumulating condition levels

the-dark-eye.rule.heat-level-and-hyperth.name: Heat Level and Hyperthermia

effect.summary: Heat Level minus water and modifiers determines hyperthermia accumulation; extreme levels can cause LP loss.

the-dark-eye.rule.heat-level-and-hyperth.cost_or_limit: Heat has four levels; water reduces the level, while exertion, sun, and humid jungle conditions raise it.
the-dark-eye.rule.heat-level-and-hyperth.go_wrong: Severe exposure can cause heatstroke or dehydration and death.
the-dark-eye.rule.heat-level-and-hyperth.combines: Rest, cooling, and water remove one level per hour.
the-dark-eye.rule.heat-level-and-hyperth.mechanism: Exposure thresholds and accumulating condition levels

the-dark-eye.rule.visibility-restriction.name: Visibility restrictions

effect.summary: Darkness, fog, or foliage impose visibility levels that penalize checks and attacks; the worst level prevents sight.

the-dark-eye.rule.visibility-restriction.cost_or_limit: Effects vary by level from minor penalties to invisibility.
the-dark-eye.rule.visibility-restriction.go_wrong: Complete darkness or sudden blindness can make checks impossible.
the-dark-eye.rule.visibility-restriction.who_may: Characters in obstructed or poorly lit conditions.
the-dark-eye.rule.visibility-restriction.combines: The GM determines which checks are affected.

the-dark-eye.rule.carrying-and-lifting-c.name: Carrying and Lifting Capacity

effect.summary: Carrying above STR × 4 pounds adds Encumbrance; short-term lifting and carrying limits and a strength-check bonus are specified.

the-dark-eye.rule.carrying-and-lifting-c.cost_or_limit: Extra Encumbrance applies per additional 8 pounds; humans, elves, and dwarves can briefly lift up to STR × 20 pounds, plus QL × 10 on a successful check.
the-dark-eye.rule.carrying-and-lifting-c.who_may: Heroes; the stated lifting limit names humans, elves, and dwarves.

the-dark-eye.rule.strategic-movement.name: Strategic Movement

effect.summary: Travel mode determines a typical daily distance, reduced by rough terrain or difficult conditions.

the-dark-eye.rule.strategic-movement.cost_or_limit: Foot march 20 miles, coach 25, horseback 30, and sea voyage 60 per day; a Middenmile equals 1,094 yards.
the-dark-eye.rule.strategic-movement.go_wrong: Rough terrain and raging seas reduce travel rates.
the-dark-eye.rule.strategic-movement.combines: Road, water, terrain, and complications affect the rate.

the-dark-eye.rule.chases.name: Chases

effect.summary: Pursuer and quarry accumulate skill points through running checks, with terrain modifying effective movement.

the-dark-eye.rule.chases.cost_or_limit: Usually at most five combat rounds; the pursuer starts with a target equal to the initial distance in yards.
the-dark-eye.rule.chases.go_wrong: If the pursuer has not accumulated the required points by the limit, the quarry escapes.
the-dark-eye.rule.chases.combines: Terrain sets effective movement; each side's points adjust the remaining target.

the-dark-eye.rule.jumping-limits.name: Jumping limits

effect.summary: Body Control checks govern high and long jumps, with distance-based penalties and maximum ranges.

the-dark-eye.rule.jumping-limits.cost_or_limit: Running long jump maximum eight yards; high jump maximum four yards; dwarves halve distances, and standing jumps take an extra penalty.
the-dark-eye.rule.jumping-limits.go_wrong: Failed checks can prevent the attempted jump.
the-dark-eye.rule.jumping-limits.combines: The optional exact-distance rule derives jumps from movement, agility, and skill points.

the-dark-eye.rule.structural-damage.name: Structural Damage

effect.summary: Weapon damage removes an object's structure points; at zero, it is destroyed or breached.

the-dark-eye.rule.structural-damage.cost_or_limit: Some weapons cannot damage particular objects; the GM decides. Attacking an inanimate object takes one action and no attack roll.
the-dark-eye.rule.structural-damage.go_wrong: A weapon may be unsuitable to damage the object.
the-dark-eye.rule.structural-damage.combines: Object durability is measured in structure points.

the-dark-eye.rule.maximum-stat-or-maximu.name: Maximum Stat or Maximum Increase

effect.summary: Improvement caps restrict combat techniques, LP, AE, KP, skills, spells, and liturgical ratings according to linked attributes or special knowledge.

the-dark-eye.rule.maximum-stat-or-maximu.cost_or_limit: Spell and chant ratings normally cap at 14; several other caps are attribute-based.
the-dark-eye.rule.maximum-stat-or-maximu.combines: Property Knowledge and Aspect Knowledge allow the specified spell or chant cap to be exceeded.

the-dark-eye.rule.permanent-loss-of-arca.name: Permanent Loss of Arcane Energy

effect.summary: Artifact creation can permanently reduce maximum AE, which does not regenerate; spent maximum can be bought back.

the-dark-eye.rule.permanent-loss-of-arca.cost_or_limit: Buying back permanent AE costs 2 AP per point; all lost AE must be restored before improving AE.
the-dark-eye.rule.permanent-loss-of-arca.go_wrong: The lost AE does not regenerate on its own.
the-dark-eye.rule.permanent-loss-of-arca.who_may: Spellcasters creating magical artifacts or otherwise losing AE permanently.
the-dark-eye.rule.permanent-loss-of-arca.where_from: Magical artifact creation or another permanent-loss cause.
the-dark-eye.rule.permanent-loss-of-arca.combines: AE improvement is barred until all permanent loss is bought back.
the-dark-eye.rule.permanent-loss-of-arca.blocked_reason: Permanent AE expenditure tied to artifact creation requires item-linked power or creation mechanics beyond the basic grammar.

the-dark-eye.rule.permanent-loss-of-karm.name: Permanent Loss of Karma Energy

effect.summary: Sacred artifact creation can permanently reduce maximum KP, which does not regenerate; spent maximum can be bought back.

the-dark-eye.rule.permanent-loss-of-karm.cost_or_limit: Buying back permanent KP costs 2 AP per point; all lost KP must be restored before improving KP.
the-dark-eye.rule.permanent-loss-of-karm.go_wrong: The lost KP does not regenerate on its own.
the-dark-eye.rule.permanent-loss-of-karm.who_may: Blessed Ones creating sacred artifacts or otherwise losing KP permanently.
the-dark-eye.rule.permanent-loss-of-karm.where_from: Sacred artifact creation or another permanent-loss cause.
the-dark-eye.rule.permanent-loss-of-karm.combines: KP improvement is barred until all permanent loss is bought back.
the-dark-eye.rule.permanent-loss-of-karm.blocked_reason: Permanent KP expenditure tied to sacred artifact creation requires item-linked power or creation mechanics beyond the basic grammar.

the-dark-eye.rule.demon-manifestation-an.name: Demon manifestation and return

effect.summary: A summoned demon manifests physically using the summoner's arcane energy, then eventually returns to its originating Sphere.

the-dark-eye.rule.demon-manifestation-an.cost_or_limit: Demons cannot remain in the Third Sphere permanently and have almost no mass.
the-dark-eye.rule.demon-manifestation-an.go_wrong: When slain, no body remains apart from a little residue.
the-dark-eye.rule.demon-manifestation-an.mind: The demon's will shapes and guides its body.
the-dark-eye.rule.demon-manifestation-an.combines: Demons are not blown or carried by wind against their will.
the-dark-eye.rule.demon-manifestation-an.blocked_reason: Summoning and constructing a creature's body from a summoner's energy are beyond the basic effect grammar.

the-dark-eye.rule.demon-damage-and-immun.name: Demon damage and immunities

effect.summary: Mundane weapons deal half damage after protection; opposing-deity-blessed weapons deal double, while other blessed or magical weapons deal normal damage.

the-dark-eye.rule.demon-damage-and-immun.cost_or_limit: Demons ignore conditions, poisons, diseases, healing, illusion, influence, and transformation spells; they cannot benefit from liturgical chants.
the-dark-eye.rule.demon-damage-and-immun.combines: Spirit modifies most spells and adds spell protection; it is doubled when already used as a modifier, and added to Toughness where Toughness applies.
the-dark-eye.rule.demon-damage-and-immun.blocked_reason: The rule combines target-specific spell immunities with weapon-source damage multipliers and interacting resistance statistics.

the-dark-eye.rule.opposing-elements.name: Opposing elements

effect.summary: Fire opposes water, air opposes ore, and humus opposes ice; elementals of opposing kinds are usually hostile but seldom fight.

the-dark-eye.rule.opposing-elements.blocked_reason: The rule can be represented as a relation between elemental types.

the-dark-eye.rule.elemental-general-rule.name: Elemental general rules

effect.summary: Elementals resist mundane and blessed attacks, resist several spell types, use Spirit in spell defenses, resist poison and disease, and interact unusually with elemental damage.

the-dark-eye.rule.elemental-general-rule.cost_or_limit: Attacks with mundane or blessed weapons do half damage; magical weapons do normal damage. Spell modifiers depend on Spirit and Toughness.
the-dark-eye.rule.elemental-general-rule.go_wrong: Opposing-element attacks are more effective; opposing-element damage spells ignore PRO.
the-dark-eye.rule.elemental-general-rule.mind: Elemental spirits have animal-like minds; djinn are intelligent and headstrong.
the-dark-eye.rule.elemental-general-rule.who_may: All elementals; djinn also know spells of their own element.
the-dark-eye.rule.elemental-general-rule.combines: Elemental immunities, opposing elements, spell modifiers, and djinn spell knowledge interact.
the-dark-eye.rule.elemental-general-rule.blocked_reason: The multiple immunity, resistance, and opposing-element interactions exceed the basic effect grammar.

the-dark-eye.rule.mundane-animals-resemb.name: Mundane animals resemble Earth animals

effect.summary: Aventuria's ordinary animals generally differ little from animals found on Earth.

the-dark-eye.rule.mundane-animals-resemb.blocked_reason: This descriptive rule requires no special game effect.

the-dark-eye.rule.familiar-bonuses.name: Familiar bonuses

effect.summary: Animals serving as witches' familiars are superior to ordinary members of their species and receive bonuses.

the-dark-eye.rule.familiar-bonuses.cost_or_limit: Specific bonuses are referred to another page and are not given here.
the-dark-eye.rule.familiar-bonuses.combines: Can use the listed animal statistics as ordinary versions without the familiar bonuses.
the-dark-eye.rule.familiar-bonuses.blocked_reason: The passage does not specify what bonuses familiars receive.

effect.summary: Ten kreutzers make a haler, ten halers a silverthaler, and ten silverthalers a ducat.
A pound is 16 ounces, a stone 14 pounds, a boulder 500 pounds, and a ton 2,000 pounds.
A hand is four inches, a foot twelve inches, a yard three feet, and a mile 1,094 paces.

the-dark-eye.rule.mages-weapon-and-armor.name: Mages' weapon and armor restrictions

effect.summary: Guild mages may carry only staves and daggers without a guild dispensation, and may wear at most gambesons.

the-dark-eye.rule.mages-weapon-and-armor.cost_or_limit: Special dispensations are rarely granted; the Gareth Academy of Sword & Staff is an exception.
the-dark-eye.rule.mages-weapon-and-armor.go_wrong: Illegal possession may violate the Codex Albyricus.
the-dark-eye.rule.mages-weapon-and-armor.combines: Some ceremonial church weapons have separate legal restrictions.
the-dark-eye.rule.mages-weapon-and-armor.blocked_reason: This is a straightforward restriction on permitted equipment.

the-dark-eye.rule.church-weapon-restrict.name: Church weapon restriction

effect.summary: Certain church-made ceremonial weapons may legally be wielded only by people appointed by their church.

the-dark-eye.rule.church-weapon-restrict.cost_or_limit: Use is limited to church-appointed individuals.
the-dark-eye.rule.church-weapon-restrict.go_wrong: Unauthorized carrying or use is unlawful.
the-dark-eye.rule.church-weapon-restrict.blocked_reason: This is a straightforward restriction on permitted equipment.

the-dark-eye.rule.two-handed-use-of-one-.name: Two-handed use of one-handed weapons

effect.summary: Using a one-handed weapon in both hands adds one damage and subtracts one Parry.

the-dark-eye.rule.two-handed-use-of-one-.cost_or_limit: Grip changes require no action but are allowed only on the user's Initiative; this rule excludes daggers and fencing weapons.
the-dark-eye.rule.two-handed-use-of-one-.blocked_reason: The effect is a direct numerical modifier.

the-dark-eye.rule.iron-forest-crossbow-c.name: Iron Forest crossbow clip

effect.summary: A clip holds ten bolts and reduces reloading time for the Iron Forest crossbow.

the-dark-eye.rule.iron-forest-crossbow-c.cost_or_limit: Changing the clip takes 10 actions; shots take 2 actions.
the-dark-eye.rule.iron-forest-crossbow-c.combines: Requires an Iron Forest crossbow and its clip.
the-dark-eye.rule.iron-forest-crossbow-c.blocked_reason: The clip's capacity and action timing are direct quantities.

the-dark-eye.rule.armor-protection-and-e.name: Armor protection and encumbrance

effect.summary: Armor grants protection and may impose encumbrance and movement or initiative penalties.

the-dark-eye.rule.armor-protection-and-e.cost_or_limit: Protection, encumbrance, penalties, weight, and cost vary by armor type.
the-dark-eye.rule.armor-protection-and-e.go_wrong: Heavy armor can reduce movement or initiative.
the-dark-eye.rule.armor-protection-and-e.blocked_reason: Protection and penalties can be represented as numerical modifiers.

the-dark-eye.rule.metal-armor-undercloth.name: Metal armor underclothes

effect.summary: Padded underclothes are required beneath metal armor.

the-dark-eye.rule.metal-armor-undercloth.blocked_reason: This is a simple equipment requirement.

the-dark-eye.rule.sheaths-and-quivers-fo.name: Sheaths and quivers for quick use

effect.summary: Without a fitted sheath or quiver, heroes usually cannot use Quickdraw or Quickload.

the-dark-eye.rule.sheaths-and-quivers-fo.cost_or_limit: The relevant fitted accessory is required for the corresponding ability.
the-dark-eye.rule.sheaths-and-quivers-fo.go_wrong: The quick-use ability is unavailable without the accessory.
the-dark-eye.rule.sheaths-and-quivers-fo.who_may: Weapon users with the relevant ability.
the-dark-eye.rule.sheaths-and-quivers-fo.combines: Sheaths pair with Quickdraw; quivers with Quickload.
the-dark-eye.rule.sheaths-and-quivers-fo.blocked_reason: This is a straightforward dependency on equipment.

the-dark-eye.rule.provisions-ration.name: Provisions ration

effect.summary: One ration supplies one person with food for one day; hunted or scavenged food counts equivalently.

the-dark-eye.rule.provisions-ration.combines: Hunted or scavenged food can substitute for a ration.
the-dark-eye.rule.provisions-ration.blocked_reason: The rule is a simple quantity-to-duration conversion.

the-dark-eye.rule.illumination-area.name: Illumination area

effect.summary: Light reduces or removes darkness penalties within its area.

the-dark-eye.rule.illumination-area.cost_or_limit: Usually covers a sphere 21–30 feet in diameter; GM sets the reach.
the-dark-eye.rule.illumination-area.blocked_reason: The basic effect grammar does not specify illumination radii or darkness penalties.

the-dark-eye.rule.burning-time.name: Burning Time

effect.summary: Measures how long a light source works without replenishment.

the-dark-eye.rule.burning-time.cost_or_limit: Ends when the stated duration runs out or supplies require replenishment.
the-dark-eye.rule.burning-time.blocked_reason: A duration limit can be represented as an item rule.

the-dark-eye.rule.sewing-serious-cuts.name: Sewing serious cuts

effect.summary: Serious cuts cannot be sewn without bandages and a sewing kit.

the-dark-eye.rule.sewing-serious-cuts.cost_or_limit: Requires bandages and a sewing kit.
the-dark-eye.rule.sewing-serious-cuts.blocked_reason: This is a direct equipment prerequisite.

the-dark-eye.rule.basic-regeneration-for.name: Basic regeneration for 6 hours of sleep

effect.summary: A full night’s sleep restores 1D6 Life, Arcane, and Karma points.

the-dark-eye.rule.basic-regeneration-for.go_wrong: Interrupted or adverse rest can reduce recovery.
the-dark-eye.rule.basic-regeneration-for.blocked_reason: Recovery can be represented as adding vitality.

the-dark-eye.rule.poor-campsite-failed-s.name: Poor campsite, failed Survival (Find Campsite) check

effect.summary: Reduces nightly recovery of Life, Arcane, and Karma points by one.

the-dark-eye.rule.poor-campsite-failed-s.cost_or_limit: Applies after a failed campsite-finding check.
the-dark-eye.rule.poor-campsite-failed-s.blocked_reason: The rule adjusts the amount of recovered resources.

the-dark-eye.rule.interruption-of-nightl.name: Interruption of nightly rest

effect.summary: A brief disturbance reduces each listed recovery by one.

the-dark-eye.rule.interruption-of-nightl.cost_or_limit: Applies to interruptions such as a dog watch.

the-dark-eye.rule.lengthier-interruption.name: Lengthier interruption of nightly rest

effect.summary: A lengthy disruption reduces each listed recovery by two.

the-dark-eye.rule.lengthier-interruption.cost_or_limit: Applies to sentry duty or a night ambush.

the-dark-eye.rule.hero-is-diseased-poiso.name: Hero is diseased/poisoned

effect.summary: Disease or poison prevents Life Point recovery.

the-dark-eye.rule.hero-is-diseased-poiso.blocked_reason: The rule blocks a stated form of recovery.

the-dark-eye.rule.good-accommodations-si.name: Good accommodations (single room in an inn)

effect.summary: Good lodging adds one to each listed recovery.

the-dark-eye.rule.good-accommodations-si.blocked_reason: The rule adjusts the amount of recovered resources.

the-dark-eye.rule.bad-surroundings-wet-c.name: Bad surroundings (wet, cold)

effect.summary: Bad conditions halve listed recovery.

the-dark-eye.rule.bad-surroundings-wet-c.cost_or_limit: Applies in wet or cold surroundings.
the-dark-eye.rule.bad-surroundings-wet-c.blocked_reason: The rule changes the amount of recovered resources.

effect.summary: Extremely bad weather prevents listed recovery.

the-dark-eye.rule.per-2-full-pounds-of-i.name: Per 2 full pounds of iron carried on the body

effect.summary: Each two pounds of carried iron reduces Arcane Energy by one.

the-dark-eye.rule.per-2-full-pounds-of-i.cost_or_limit: Every full two pounds carried costs one Arcane Energy.
the-dark-eye.rule.per-2-full-pounds-of-i.blocked_reason: The rule subtracts a resource according to carried weight.
